transliteration_key.ch: چ / ج بصوت تش (ضمير المخاطبة المؤنثة في الخليج)

phrases.arabic: مَا قَدَرْت أَرُدّ عَلَيْك قَبِل شْوَي

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: هلا سامر، معاك مريم
dialogue.english: Hi Samer, it's Mariam.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: هلا والله مريم، شو علومج؟
dialogue.english: Hi Mariam, what's new?

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: الحمد لله طيبة. اتصلت عليك قبل شوي بس الخط كان مشغول
dialogue.transliteration: il7amdulillah tayyiba. ittasalt 3aleek gabl shwayy bas il-khatt kaan mashghuul
dialogue.english: All good, thank God. I called you a bit ago but the line was busy.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: إي، كنت أكلم أخوي. آسف ما قدرت أرد عليج
dialogue.transliteration: ee, kint akallim akhooy. aasif ma gdart arudd 3aleech
dialogue.english: Yeah, I was talking with my brother. Sorry I couldn't answer you.

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: لا عليك. أبي أكلمك عن الموعد
dialogue.english: Don't worry about it. I want to talk to you about the appointment.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: تفضلي، بس ثانية، رصيدي بيخلص
dialogue.english: Go ahead, just a second, my credit is about to run out.

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: طيب خلني أتكلم بسرعة قبل لا ينقطع الخط
dialogue.transliteration: tayyib khalni atkallam bsur3a gabl la yingati3 il-khatt
dialogue.english: Okay, let me talk fast before the call cuts off.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: لا لا، خلاص، انقطع. تقدرين تتصلين علي بعد شوي؟
dialogue.transliteration: laa laa, khalaas, ingata3. tigdareen titsileen 3alay ba3d shwayy?
dialogue.english: No no, that's it, it got cut off. Can you call me back in a bit?

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: تمام، زين إنك اتصلت أصلا. باتصل عليك
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, zeen innak ittasalt aslan. baatsil 3aleek
dialogue.english: Okay, good that you called at all. I'll call you back.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: الله يعافيج، أنتظرج
dialogue.english: Thank you, I'll wait for you.

pair.english: Can you call me back in a bit?

lessons.culture: A Gulf call often opens with "هلا" or "ألو", and "السلام عليكم" is common too, especially with someone older; a short warm greeting like "شو علومك؟" comes before the reason for the call. Ending with "الله يعافيك" or "في أمان الله" keeps it polite.

exercises.prompt: You pick up the phone and hear: "ألو؟". Answer naturally, asking who is calling.

too_formal.item: السلام عليكم، من فضلك من المتصل؟
too_formal.feedback: This is correct Arabic, but far more formal than the ordinary way of answering the phone.

exercises.tip: "منو" (Kuwait and much of the Gulf) or "مين" both mean who; "معاي" is "with me", so "منو معاي" is "who is with me" on the line.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks you on the phone: "شو علومك؟". Say that everything is fine, thank God.

too_formal.item: الأمور على ما يرام، ولله الحمد
too_formal.feedback: Correct but bookish; a spoken reply is much shorter.

exercises.tip: "الحمد لله" almost always appears in the answer. A woman says "طيبة".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "ما قدرت _____ عليك قبل شوي." Meaning: I couldn't answer you a bit ago.

too_formal.feedback: Understandable, but "رد على" is the word actually used for answering someone's call.

exercises.tip: "قدرت" is said "gdart" in the Gulf, because ق is pronounced like a hard g.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "الخط _____ علي وأنا أتكلم معاك." Meaning: The call got cut off on me while I was talking to you.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but sounds like a technical report, not something a person says on the phone.

exercises.tip: "انقطع الخط علي" is the everyday way to say a call dropped on you.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Gulf Arabic: "My battery died."

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically fine, but far more formal than how people actually say it.

exercises.tip: "خلص" / "خلصت" covers running out of almost anything: credit, battery, petrol.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "There's no signal here."

too_formal.item: لا توجد تغطية شبكية في هذا المكان
too_formal.feedback: Correct but reads like a technician's report, not spoken Gulf Arabic.

exercises.tip: "شبكة" is the everyday word for phone signal; "هني" is the Gulf "here" ("هنا" is also heard).

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "My credit ran out"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but "خلص" is the word used in everyday speech, not "انتهى".

exercises.tip: "رصيد" is prepaid phone credit.

exercises.prompt: Which is the natural way to answer an incoming call?

too_formal.item: السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته، من المتصل؟
too_formal.feedback: Too long for picking up a phone; the short "ألو" or "هلا" is what is said.

exercises.tip: "ألو" answers the phone; the other phrases come once the call is already going.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "مشغول / كان / الخط".

too_formal.feedback: That would be an unusual, technical way to say the line was busy.

exercises.tip: "الخط" comes first, then "كان", then how the line was.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "علي / بعد شوي / تتصل / تقدر".

too_formal.item: هل بإمكانك معاودة الاتصال بي لاحقاً
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but this is the formal written version, not the spoken order of words.

exercises.tip: "اتصل علي" (call on me) is how the Gulf says "call me".

reply.english: In front of the main entrance.

phrases.english: We'll meet at the Grand Mosque.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: مريم، وين نتلاقى باجر؟
dialogue.english: Mariam, where should we meet tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: شرايك نتلاقى في الكافيه اللي عند المجمع؟
dialogue.transliteration: shraayak nitlaagaa fi l-kaafeeh illi 3ind il-mujamma3?
dialogue.english: What do you think, shall we meet at the cafe near the mall?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: فكرة زينة. الساعة كم تناسبج؟
dialogue.english: Good idea. What time suits you?

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: طيب وين بالضبط؟ قدام الكافيه؟
dialogue.english: Okay, where exactly? In front of the cafe?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: إي، أشوفج عند المدخل الرئيسي
dialogue.english: Yes, I'll see you at the main entrance.

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: تمام، بكون هناك قبلك أكيد
dialogue.english: Great, I'll definitely be there before you.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: لا تتأخرين علي يا مريم
dialogue.english: Don't be late on me, Mariam.

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: ولا يهمك، وإذا تأخرت باتصل عليك
dialogue.transliteration: wala yhimmak, w idha ta2akhkharit baatsil 3aleek
dialogue.english: Don't worry, and if I'm late I'll call you.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: ماشي، أشوفج باجر
dialogue.english: Okay, see you tomorrow.

response.english: In front of the main entrance.

pair.english: What do you think, shall we go together?

lessons.culture: In the UAE and Kuwait people usually arrange to meet at a mall, a well-known cafe or a big mosque rather than giving a street address. The Umayyad Mosque is in Damascus, so the Gulf line names a local landmark instead, such as the Grand Mosque in Kuwait or the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque in Abu Dhabi.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks you: "وين نتلاقى؟". Suggest meeting at the cafe.

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically correct, but far more formal than a casual suggestion.

exercises.tip: "خلنا" + verb is the everyday way to suggest doing something together.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "الساعة كم تناسبك؟". Say that 7 o'clock is good for you.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but sounds like a written appointment confirmation, not spoken.

exercises.tip: "زين" (masculine) and "زينة" (feminine, so it agrees with "ساعة") mean good in the Gulf.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "أشوفك _____ المدخل الرئيسي." Meaning: I'll see you at the main entrance.

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but "قدام" or "عند" is what is actually said, not "أمام".

exercises.tip: "قدام" is pronounced "gidaam" in the Gulf and means in front of.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "إذا _____ اتصل علي." Meaning: If you're late, call me.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but very formal written Arabic, not how it is said.

exercises.tip: "إذا" + past-tense verb is the everyday conditional.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Gulf Arabic: "Don't be late."

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but this is a formal written notice style, not spoken Gulf Arabic.

exercises.tip: "لا" + present-tense verb is the everyday negative command; add "علي" to mean "don't keep me waiting".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'll be there before you."

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically identical but uses the formal future "سـ" instead of the spoken "ب".

exercises.tip: "ب" + present-tense verb makes the everyday future; in Kuwait "راح" + verb is also common.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence asks "What time suits you?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct but stiffer than the everyday spoken question.

exercises.tip: "الساعة كم" (what hour) is the everyday Gulf way to ask about time.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Let's meet at the cafe"?

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically correct classical form, but not how it's said in conversation.

exercises.tip: "خلنا" + present-tense verb is the everyday "let's".

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "سبعة / زينة / الساعة".

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but far more elaborate than the short spoken question.

exercises.tip: The time comes first, then the check word "زينة" at the end.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "المدخل الرئيسي / عند / أشوفك".

too_formal.item: سألتقي بك أمام المدخل الرئيسي للمبنى
too_formal.feedback: Correct but a much longer, written-style sentence.

exercises.tip: "أشوفك" (I'll see you) usually opens the sentence, then the place.

phrases.arabic: خَلْنَا نْشُوف يُوم يِنَاسِبْنَا اِحْنَا الثِّنَيْن
phrases.transliteration: khalna nshoof yoom yinaasibna i7na ith-thnayn

phrases.arabic: نِقْدَر نِتْلَاقَى بَعْد الظُّهْر بِدْل الصُّبْح؟
phrases.transliteration: nigdar nitlaagaa ba3d idh-dhuhr badal is-sub7?

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: ألو سامر، أبي أغير موعدنا اليوم
dialogue.transliteration: aloo Saamer, abi aghayyir maw3idna l-yoom
dialogue.english: Hello Samer, I want to change our appointment today.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: شو صار؟ فيه شي؟
dialogue.english: What happened? Is something wrong?

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: إي، عندي ظرف في البيت وما أقدر أجي اليوم
dialogue.transliteration: ee, 3indi dhurf fi l-beet w ma agdar aji l-yoom
dialogue.english: Yeah, something came up at home and I can't come today.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: لا عليج. ممكن نأجله لباجر؟
dialogue.english: Don't worry about it. Can we postpone to tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: ما في مشكلة، نأجله لباجر. بس نقدر نتلاقى بعد الظهر بدل الصبح؟
dialogue.transliteration: ma fee mushkila, ni2ajjilah la-baajir. bas nigdar nitlaagaa ba3d idh-dhuhr badal is-sub7?
dialogue.english: No problem, we'll postpone to tomorrow. But can we meet in the afternoon instead of the morning?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: تمام، بعد الظهر أحسن لي بعد
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, ba3d idh-dhuhr a7san li ba3ad
dialogue.english: Great, the afternoon is better for me too.

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: الله يعافيك، آسفة على التغيير المفاجئ
dialogue.english: Thanks, sorry for the sudden change.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: لا عليج، عادي. المكان للحين نفسه؟
dialogue.english: Don't worry, it's fine. Is the place still the same place?

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: لا، غيرنا المكان، بنتلاقى عند الكافيه الجديد
dialogue.transliteration: laa, ghayyarna l-makaan, binitlaagaa 3ind il-kaafeeh ij-jadeed
dialogue.english: No, we changed the place, we'll meet at the new cafe.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: ماشي، بحفظ الموقع. مشكورة إنج خبرتيني بدري
dialogue.transliteration: maashi, ba7fadh il-mawgi3. mashkoora inch khabbarteeni badri
dialogue.english: Okay, I'll save the location. Thanks for letting me know early.

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: الله يعافيك، أشوفك باجر بعد الظهر
dialogue.transliteration: allah y3aafeek, ashoofak baajir ba3d idh-dhuhr
dialogue.english: You're welcome, see you tomorrow afternoon.

pair.english: I want to change the appointment.

pair.arabic: نِقْدَر نِتْلَاقَى بَعْد الظُّهْر بِدْل الصُّبْح؟
pair.transliteration: nigdar nitlaagaa ba3d idh-dhuhr badal is-sub7?
pair.english: Can we meet in the afternoon instead of the morning?

response.english: Yes, the afternoon is better for me.

pair.english: Is the place still the same place?

lessons.culture: Plans shift often around work, family visits and prayer times, and rearranging at short notice is normal as long as it comes with a quick apology like "آسف على التغيير المفاجئ". The other person usually answers "لا عليك" or "عادي", and Friday plans are usually set around the Friday prayer.

exercises.prompt: Your friend says: "آسف على التغيير المفاجئ". Tell them not to worry about it.

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but far more formal than the short spoken reassurance.

exercises.tip: "لا عليك" (to a man) or "لا عليج" (to a woman) is the standard easy way to say "don't worry about it".

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "ممكن نأجله لباجر؟". Agree, saying no problem.

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically fine, but this is the written, not the spoken, register.

exercises.tip: "ما في مشكلة" is a very common easy agreement phrase.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "عندي _____ وما أقدر أجي." Meaning: Something came up for me and I can't come.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but redundant and bookish; the spoken version is much shorter.

exercises.tip: "عندي ظرف" is the everyday Gulf way to say something has come up.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "نقدر نتلاقى بعد الظهر _____ الصبح؟" Meaning: Can we meet in the afternoon instead of the morning?

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but more formal than the short spoken "بدل".

exercises.tip: "بدل" means "instead of" in everyday speech.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Gulf Arabic: "I can't come today."

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically correct but more formal than the everyday spoken phrase.

exercises.tip: "ما أقدر" is the everyday "I can't"; ق sounds like g, so it is said "agdar".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Can we postpone to tomorrow?"

too_formal.item: هل يمكننا تأجيل الموعد إلى الغد؟
too_formal.feedback: Correct but a longer, written-style question.

exercises.tip: "باجر" is the Gulf word for tomorrow; "بكرة" is also understood.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Is the place still the same place?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but more formal phrasing than the spoken question.

exercises.tip: "للحين" means "still, up to now" in Gulf speech.

exercises.prompt: Which is a natural apology for changing plans suddenly?

too_formal.item: أعتذر منكم عن هذا التغيير الطارئ
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but stiff and overly formal for a friend.

exercises.tip: "آسف" (man) / "آسفة" (woman) على التغيير المفاجئ fits a casual apology.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "لباجر / نأجله / ممكن".

too_formal.item: هل من الممكن أن نؤجل الأمر إلى الغد
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but a much longer formal question.

exercises.tip: "ممكن" opens the question, then the verb, then the day.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "الصبح / بدل / بعد الظهر / نتلاقى / نقدر".
exercises.answer: نقدر نتلاقى بعد الظهر بدل الصبح
accepted: نقدر نتلاقى بعد الظهر بدل الصبح
نقدر نتلاقى بعد الظهر عوض الصبح
nigdar nitlaagaa ba3d idh-dhuhr badal is-sub7

too_formal.item: هل بإمكاننا اللقاء بعد الظهيرة عوضاً عن الصباح؟
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but a longer, more formal question.

exercises.tip: "نقدر" (can we) opens it, then the verb, then the two times being compared.

reply.english: Sure, what do you want to tell him?

phrases.english: Can you pass him a message?

phrases.arabic: بَوَصِّل لِه اِلْخَبَر أَوِّل مَا يِدْخِل
phrases.transliteration: bawassil lah il-khabar awwal ma yidkhal

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: لا، مب هني الحين، راح المجمع
dialogue.transliteration: laa, mub hni l-7een, raa7 il-mujamma3
dialogue.english: No, he's not here right now, he went to the mall.

dialogue.speaker: Rashid
dialogue.arabic: آه، متى يرجع تقريبا؟
dialogue.english: Ah, roughly when will he be back?

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: ما أدري بالضبط، بعد شوي إن شاء الله
dialogue.transliteration: ma adri bi-dh-dhabt, ba3d shwayy in shaa2 allah
dialogue.english: I don't know exactly, in a bit God willing.

dialogue.speaker: Rashid
dialogue.arabic: طيب ممكن توصلين له رسالة؟
dialogue.english: Okay, can you pass a message to him for me?

dialogue.speaker: Rashid
dialogue.arabic: قولي له راشد اتصل، ويتصل علي إذا فاضي
dialogue.transliteration: gooli lah Raashid ittasal, w yitsil 3alay idha faadi
dialogue.english: Tell him Rashid called, and to call me if he's free.

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: طيب، بقول له أول ما يوصل
dialogue.transliteration: tayyib, bagool lah awwal ma yoosal
dialogue.english: Okay, I'll tell him as soon as he arrives.

dialogue.speaker: Rashid
dialogue.arabic: عنده رقمي؟
dialogue.english: Does he have my number?

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: ما أدري، خلني آخذ رقمك احتياط
dialogue.transliteration: ma adri, khalni aakhudh ragmak i7tiyaat
dialogue.english: I don't know, let me take your number just in case.

dialogue.speaker: Rashid
dialogue.arabic: تفضلي، يعطيك العافية على هالمعروف
dialogue.english: Here you go, thanks a lot for the favor.

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: الله يعافيك، بوصل له الخبر أول ما يدخل
dialogue.transliteration: allah y3aafeek, bawassil lah il-khabar awwal ma yidkhal
dialogue.english: You're very welcome, I'll pass him the news as soon as he's in.

response.english: No, he's not here right now.
I don't know exactly, in a bit.

pair.english: Can you take a message for me?

response.english: Sure, what do you want to tell him?

lessons.culture: It is normal in the Gulf for a family member to answer the phone and pass on a message, and men often ask after the family before the message itself. "يعطيك العافية" is the standard thank-you for a favor, and "الله يعافيك" is the usual reply.

exercises.prompt: Someone calling asks: "سامر موجود؟" but he is out. Say he's not here right now.

too_formal.item: لا، إنه غير متواجد في الوقت الحالي
too_formal.feedback: Grammatically correct but sounds like an office receptionist, not a spoken reply.

exercises.tip: "مب" (UAE) and "مو" (Kuwait) both mean "not"; "الحين" is the Gulf "now".

exercises.prompt: Someone asks you: "ممكن توصل له رسالة؟" Agree and ask what they want to say.

too_formal.item: بالتأكيد، ما الذي تريد أن تخبره به؟
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but far more formal than the everyday phrasing.

exercises.tip: "تبي" (you want) is the Gulf form; "تريد" is the formal one.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "_____ له يتصل علي." Meaning: Tell him to call me.

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically correct but a written-style instruction, not the short spoken one.

exercises.tip: "قول له" is the everyday "tell him"; ق sounds like g, so it is "gool".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "بقول له _____ ما يوصل." Meaning: I'll tell him as soon as he arrives.

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but a more formal written order of the sentence.

exercises.tip: "أول ما" is the everyday way to say "as soon as".

exercises.prompt: Translate into Gulf Arabic: "Do you have my number?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct but more formal wording than the short spoken question.

exercises.tip: "عندك" / "معك" both work for "do you have" in everyday speech.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Thanks a lot."

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but far more formal than the everyday "يعطيك العافية".

exercises.tip: "يعطيك العافية" is one of the most common everyday thank-yous, and "مشكور" is a short one.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence asks "When will he be back?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but the future "سـ" and "يعود" are the written form; speech says "يرجع".

exercises.tip: "متى" and "شحين" both mean when in Gulf speech.

exercises.prompt: Which is the natural reply to "يعطيك العافية"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but a more formal set phrase than the everyday reply.

exercises.tip: "الله يعافيك" is the standard reply to a thank-you; to a woman it is "الله يعافيج".

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "رسالة / توصل له / ممكن".

too_formal.item: هل يمكن أن تنقل إليه رسالة؟
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but a longer, more formal question.

exercises.tip: "ممكن" opens the request, then the verb, then what is being asked for.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "يوصل / ما / أول / بقول له".

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but a longer written-style sentence.

exercises.tip: "بقول له" (I'll tell him) opens it, then the time clause "أول ما يوصل".

challenge.title: A Phone Call to Rearrange Plans
challenge.instructions: Write and act out a phone conversation of at least 10 lines. It must include answering the phone, proposing a place and a time to meet, changing that plan for a real reason, agreeing on a new time or place, and, if the person you called is not free, leaving a message for someone else to pass on.
required_elements: Answering the phone with ألو or هلا.
Asking or stating who is calling, using منو معاي or معاك + name.
A suggestion of where to meet, using خلنا نتلاقى or a similar phrase.
A question about time, using الساعة كم تناسبك or a similar phrase.
A reason for changing the plan, using عندي ظرف or a similar phrase.
A request to postpone or change, using ممكن نأجله or نقدر نتلاقى.
An apology for the change, using آسف على التغيير المفاجئ or a similar phrase.
A reassurance in response, using لا عليك.
A closing thank-you, using يعطيك العافية.
At least one exchange about leaving or taking a message, using رسالة or قول له.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: أَلُو؟
dialogue.english: Hello?

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: هلا سامر، معاك مريم. شو علومك؟
dialogue.english: Hi Samer, it's Mariam. What's new?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: الحمد لله طيب. شو في؟
dialogue.english: All good, thank God. What's up?

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: خلنا نتلاقى في الكافيه باجر، الساعة كم تناسبك؟
dialogue.transliteration: khalna nitlaagaa fi l-kaafeeh baajir, is-saa3a kam tinaasbak?
dialogue.english: Let's meet at the cafe tomorrow, what time suits you?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: الساعة خمسة زينة
dialogue.english: 5 o'clock is good.

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: تمام، أشوفك عند المدخل الرئيسي
dialogue.english: Great, I'll see you at the main entrance.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: آسف بس، عندي ظرف في البيت وما أقدر أجي الساعة خمسة
dialogue.transliteration: aasif bas, 3indi dhurf fi l-beet w ma agdar aji is-saa3a khamsa
dialogue.english: Sorry but, something came up at home and I can't come at 5.

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: لا عليك. ممكن نأجله للساعة سبعة؟
dialogue.english: Don't worry about it. Can we postpone to 7?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: ما في مشكلة، نأجله لسبعة. آسف على التغيير المفاجئ
dialogue.transliteration: ma fee mushkila, ni2ajjilah la-sab3a. aasif 3ala t-taghyeer il-mufaaji2
dialogue.english: No problem, we'll postpone to 7. Sorry for the sudden change.

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: لا عليك أبد. وإذا ما قدرت تجي، قول لأخوك يوصل لي رسالة
dialogue.transliteration: laa 3aleek abad. w idha ma gdart tiji, gool la-akhook yiwassil li risaala
dialogue.english: Don't worry at all. And if you can't come, tell your brother to pass me a message.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: أكيد، بقول له. يعطيك العافية على صبرك
dialogue.transliteration: akeed, bagool lah. y3aateek il-3aafya 3ala sabrak
dialogue.english: Sure, I'll tell him. Thanks a lot for your patience.

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: الله يعافيك، أشوفك الساعة سبعة
dialogue.english: You're very welcome, see you at 7.
